Errors and fixes:\n   - No source-code fix has been made yet, so there are no \"fixes\" per se — this section covers investigation errors encountered and corrected:\n     - Initial attempt to read `.mock.results[...].value` from a vitest spy (`scaleSpy.mock.results[...].value`) failed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')` because `mock.results` entries are `{type, value}` for return values, not call arguments — the spy in question captures the SELECTOR'S ARGUMENT (via `spy(selectorResult)`), so I should have used `spy.mock.calls.at(-1)?.[0]` instead. Fixed by switching from `scaleSpy.mock.results[...].value` to `scaleSpy.mock.calls.at(-1)?.[0]` (i.e., reading from `.mock.calls` not `.mock.results`), which resolved subsequent dumps correctly.\n     - Attempted `polygon = container.querySelector('.recharts-radar-polygon')` and read `.getAttribute('points')` — got `null`/`undefined` because the actual drawn shape is an SVG `<path>` (Recharts' `Polygon` component renders a `<path>` with `d`, not raw `<polygon points=...>`). Fixed by querying `.recharts-radar-polygon path` (or more precisely `.recharts-radar-polygon path.recharts-polygon` per `expectRadarPolygons.ts` helper) and reading the `d` attribute instead.\n     - First polygon dump returned a degenerate/collapsed path `M300,300L300,300L300,300L300,300L300,300Z` — this was because no `PolarRadiusAxis` with an explicit `domain={[0,100]}` was provided, so the radius scale had a mismatched/degenerate domain (likely defaulting based on auto domain not matching test data range properly, or animation-related). Fixed by adding `<PolarRadiusAxis domain={[0, 100]} />` and `isAnimationActive={false}` on `<Radar>` in the repro render, after which the polygon path showed real varying coordinates.\n     - `pip install pillow` failed (`pip: command not found`) when I attempted to inspect PNG dimensions programmatically; worked around by reading PNG headers manually via a small Python script using `struct`/`zlib` on raw bytes (`struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])`) instead of relying on Pillow, and separately used the Read tool directly on the PNG files (which renders/interprets images) to visually inspect them.\n     - A `node -e` attempt to `require('victory-vendor/d3-scale')` via a `/tmp/t.mjs` ESM file failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (module resolution only works from within the /app project root due to node_modules location) — fixed by running the equivalent CommonJS `require(...)` directly via `node -e \"...\"` (inline `-e` script) from the `/app` working directory instead of a standalone `/tmp/*.mjs` file, which succeeded (since Bash cwd was /app and CJS `require` resolves relative to cwd/module search paths correctly).\n     - No explicit user feedback/corrections were received during this session beyond the very first bug report — there have been no further user chat turns; all subsequent activity has been my own autonomous investigation via tool calls.\n\n5. Problem Solving:\n   - Solved (root cause substantially identified, pending final confirmation and fix): The bug stems from an inconsistency between how the angle-axis \"offset\" (needed to center category labels/tooltip sectors correctly within their band, for a categorical `scaleBand`-based angle axis) is computed for (a) rendered axis tick labels (`combineAxisTicks` in axisSelectors.ts) and tooltip-tick lookup (`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis` in tooltipSelectors.ts) — both of which explicitly flip the offset's sign based on `mathSign(axisRange[0] - axisRange[1])`, i.e., based on whether the angle axis range increases or decreases — versus (b) the drawn Radar polygon vertices (`computeRadarPoints` in Radar.tsx), which add `angleBandSize` sourced from `getBandSizeOfAxis` (ChartUtils.ts), a function that returns `scale.bandwidth()` directly and is ALWAYS NON-NEGATIVE, with no sign/direction awareness at all.\n   - Empirically confirmed via `node -e` scriptlets against `victory-vendor/d3-scale`'s `scaleBand` that raw `scale.map(category)` values differ from rendered axis tick-label coordinates by exactly one full bandwidth step (offset), and that this offset's sign flips with axis-range direction in the label/tooltip code paths but not in the polygon-drawing code path.\n   - Confirmed via multiple full-DOM-render experiments (varying `startAngle`/`endAngle`: default 90/-270, reversed -270/90, 0/360, 360/0, 45/405, -90/270, 270/-90, and the `reversed` prop) that:\n     - For the DEFAULT decreasing-direction configuration (90→-270, the built-in RadarChart default), the drawn polygon and axis tick labels HAPPEN TO AGREE (sign combination cancels out favorably), and hover-sweep tests (at 15° or 30° increments) resolved tooltips consistently to the correct/expected nearest label in that config.\n     - For INCREASING-direction configurations (e.g., 0→360, or reversed prop, or other reversed start/end orderings), the drawn polygon's vertex-to-label correspondence becomes WRONG (e.g., for 0→360, the polygon's \"North\" vertex renders at the TOP of the chart while the \"North\" axis tick label renders at the BOTTOM), directly reproducing the visual bug in `mismatch.png`. Hover-sweep tests in these configurations also showed inconsistent tooltip resolution relative to the rendered labels, reproducing `bug.png`.\n   - This directly explains the user's reported symptom fully: the axis labels and tooltip-hit-testing are mutually self-consistent (since they share the same offset formula/tick set), but the DRAWN SHAPE is the odd one out, using a sign-insensitive `angleBandSize`. (Note: this is somewhat in tension with the user's framing that hover ALSO disagrees with labels in bug.png; this is explained by the fact that the specific chart in bug.png may be using a non-default start/end angle configuration or `reversed`, OR — since the drawn shape is wrong, a user visually associates the WRONG shape with a label, and then hovering \"near what looks like it should be a given series' point\" naturally resolves to a different series than expected purely because the shape itself was mis-plotted; all three symptoms trace back to the single point-computation defect once you also account for label/tooltip already being correct/self-consistent in isolation).\n   - STILL OPEN / NOT YET DONE: I have not yet written or applied the actual code fix. Problem Solving:\n   - Root cause fully confirmed and fixed: `computeRadarPoints` in `Radar.tsx` was adding an always-non-negative `angleBandSize` (derived from `getBandSizeOfAxis`, which returns `scale.bandwidth()` — always positive for d3 `scaleBand` regardless of range direction) to each point's raw `scale.map(name)` angle. Meanwhile, the rendered axis tick labels (`combineAxisTicks`) and tooltip-tick lookup (`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis`) both explicitly flip the sign of this same offset based on `mathSign(axisRange[0] - axisRange[1])` (positive/decreasing range → positive offset; negative/increasing range → negative offset). This meant that for the RadarChart's default decreasing range (`startAngle=90, endAngle=-270`), the signs happened to agree and the bug was invisible; for any increasing-range configuration (e.g. `startAngle=0, endAngle=360`, or various reversed/rotated variants), the drawn polygon's vertex angles ended up shifted by a full band-width in the wrong direction relative to the axis labels and tooltip resolution — reproducing both `mismatch.png` (shape vs. label mismatch) and `bug.png` (tooltip resolving to the wrong series) simultaneously, since all three symptoms trace to this single point-computation defect.\n   - Fix implemented: compute `bandSizeSign = mathSign(range[0] - range[1])` (falling back to `1` if range is unavailable, preserving old default-direction behavior) inside `computeRadarPoints`, multiply it into `angleBandSize` before adding to the raw scale-mapped angle. The `range` value needed to reach `computeRadarPoints` was threaded through by adding a `range` field to the `AngleAxisForRadar` type and wiring `selectAngleAxisRangeWithReversed` into the `selectAngleAxisWithScaleAndViewport` selector's dependencies in `radarSelectors.ts`.\n   - Verified fix correctness three ways: (a) direct numeric comparison of tick coordinates vs. radar point angles across 7 start/end angle configurations — all matched exactly (to floating-point precision) after the fix; (b) simulated mouse hover in jsdom for the previously-broken `0/360` configuration, confirming the tooltip now resolves to the correct series (\"North\", value 100) at the screen position where North's (corrected) tick/point coincide; (c) stash/pop test to prove the new regression tests genuinely fail without the fix and pass with it.\n   - Verified RadialBar (the other polar graphical item using categorical angle axes) is not affected by the same root cause, since its centric-layout code path uses the already-correctly-signed tick coordinates via `getCateCoordinateOfBar`, not a raw unsigned bandSize addition.\n   - Ran `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` after the src changes (before adding tests) — zero type errors.\n   - Ran the full test suite (`npx vitest run`) and determined the only test failure attributable to this change was in `test/state/selectors/radarSelectors.spec.tsx`, which was then fixed. All other 8 failing test files were confirmed pre-existing/environmental and unrelated to this change (omnidoc doc-generation tests, website sitemap/routes/api-doc tests, buildOutput.test.ts checking `lib/es6/umd/types` folder contents against expectations, and a Playwright browser-not-installed error).\n   - Remaining to be done: one more full-suite run to give final confirmation that, after fixing the `radarSelectors.spec.tsx` expectation, the overall failure count is back down to only the 8 known pre-existing/unrelated failures (i.e., zero regressions caused by this fix).\n\n6. But the axis tick labels and tooltip tick lookup (`combineAxisTicks`/`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis`) apply that same offset with a sign that flips based on whether the axis range increases or decreases (`mathSign(range[0] - range[1])`). For the `RadarChart` default (`startAngle=90, endAngle=-270`, a decreasing range) the signs happened to coincide, hiding the bug — but for any increasing-range configuration (e.g. `startAngle=0, endAngle=360`), the drawn polygon vertices landed a full band-width away from where the axis label and tooltip agreed the same series should be, producing both the shape/label mismatch and the wrong-series tooltip hover reported in the bug.\n\n**Fix:** Threaded the axis range into `computeRadarPoints` (new `range` field on `AngleAxisForRadar`, wired via `selectAngleAxisRangeWithReversed` in `radarSelectors.ts`) and applied the same `mathSign`-based sign flip there, so the drawn points, axis labels, and tooltip resolution are always computed from the same signed offset.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Added 8 permanent regression tests in `test/polar/Radar.spec.tsx` covering 7 start/end angle configurations (checking polygon vertices match axis ticks) plus a jsdom hover-simulation test for the specific `0°/360°` case from the bug report.\n- Confirmed via `git stash` that these new tests fail without the fix and pass with it.\n- Fixed one incidentally-stale assertion in `test/state/selectors/radarSelectors.spec.tsx` that needed the new `range` field added to its expected object.\n- Ran the full suite (`npx vitest run`): 7247 passed, 8 failed — and confirmed via a clean-checkout stash test that all 8 failures (`scripts/buildOutput.test.ts`, 4 `omnidoc/*` files, 3 `www/test/*` website files) are pre-existing/environmental, present identically whether or not this fix is applied.
